title: The Economics of Welfare

definition.text: The Economics of Welfare is Arthur Cecil Pigou's 1920 book that introduced the idea of the externality and proposed correcting it with a tax.

facts.text: Pigou built on Alfred Marshall's idea of an externality: a cost or benefit falling on others that the person causing it does not account for.
It first planted the idea that governments should tax activities that put uncompensated costs on others, now called a Pigouvian tax.
Pigou applied the reasoning to traffic congestion, an early case of what became congestion pricing.
It argued that markets are inefficient when externalities exist, so the state must intervene.

notes: Phrase concept with no page of its own. One source (163d71c79ad7) dates a later edition 1932; the work was first published as Wealth and Welfare and retitled.

title: Conservation Reconsidered

definition.text: Conservation Reconsidered is John V. Krutilla's 1967 paper describing the economic value of undisturbed natural places such as rivers and forests.

facts.text: In it Krutilla introduced existence value, the value people get from the mere existence of something such as unspoiled wilderness or a species, even if they never use it.
This idea of 'nonuse value' made Krutilla a pioneer of environmental economics.
